chapter_note: The chapter is dominated by systematic cosmological process-description (discharge/sweeping of the three dark vessels; purification of firmaments and earths; remnant signs in the created order). The dialogue attributions (“disciples…”, “apostle…”, “enlightener…”) function as later compilation frame; once stripped, the remaining teaching stays inside the cosmic system (cosmos→cosmos mapping) with no institutional or NT overlay.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.111⟩
When the Father of Life discharged these three vessels from above, they of water and of darkness and of fire, did he perhaps discharge them to their pits at the edge of the firmament? Or did he discharge them first to this earth, and then he swept them from the earth and threw them to their places?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: “Once again the disciples questioned him, saying to him:”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A substantive cosmological question is embedded in a later Q&A frame; the frame voice (“disciples… questioned him”) marks compilation apparatus rather than the oldest impersonal exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: when the Father of Life was about to discharge these three vessels he poured the three upon this earth, one by one at its (appointed) hour and season. He discharged them and cast them down to the earth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle says to them:”) and the direct-address preface (“As for what you have asked me… you must understand this,”) as later application/teaching-management voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core process-description (timed descent of the three vessels) is introduced by a Layer-2 dialogue attribution (“apostle”) and second-person instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: Then he bailed and scooped them from this earth in these three garments, they of wind and of water and of fire, which swathed his body. He poured and made them flow into the three pits [ ... w]hich he had [es]tablished during the construc[tio]n of the worlds [ ... ] they [ ... ] something remained behind on the face of the earth from these three vessels, so that you can find their mark and type displayed in the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanics and correspondential residue (“mark and type displayed in the universe”) remain wholly within the cosmic architecture; no institutional identification or citation formula appears.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.112⟩
The element that is left in water is the pungency and the salinity of this salty inner sea that surrounds the worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmos→cosmos mapping: a residual quality in water is identified as sensory/chemical properties manifested in a cosmic sea surrounding the worlds.

paragraphs.core_text: And the remnant that is left from the darkness is this black mountain that exists in the surroundings of the sunrise. For when the sun would shine over the world no sunlight is visible there, because the darkness that gushes from it manifests above it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic geography and phenomenology (black mountain at sunrise; light blocked by exuding darkness) with no present-world polemic or institutional anchor.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.118⟩
And the remnant that remains behind from the fire, upon the earth, are all the mountains and islands from where fumes of fire gush up and are visible. For these things are the remnant of the great vessel, the vestige that was conjoined with this fire that comes up from the earth; together with the mountains and hills [ ... ] places where no fruit sprouts on the trees [ ... ] greater than that place from the limb and [ ... / ... ] the trees shall not bear fruit in that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic remnant-doctrine: dark fire’s residue is read in natural phenomena (volcanic fumes; barren zones). The “trees shall not bear fruit” functions as cosmological consequence, not NT quotation.

paragraphs.core_text: why they were not discharged from above into the ditches prepared for them (straightaway); but were firstly poured upon the earth, and afterwards were swept from the earth and cast down into their pits?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed Q&A frame and petition language (“Once again his disciples… We ask you, our master, to [make clear] and instruct us…”) retaining only the cosmological problem-statement.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The content is a structural cosmological question, but it is packaged in hagiographic classroom address (“our master”) typical of the compiled Kephalaia frame.

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life discharged these vessels from above upon the earth, he poured them out for this reason: so that also the water and the darkness and the fire that exist in these three earths would be drawn and ascend towards they that had come down from above, and the earths would be purified and cleansed. Due to this he poured these vessels down to the earth, of water and of darkness and of fire, so that also the water and darkness and fire that exist in the earths would be drawn up towards they that had descended from above.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Then the enlightener speaks to his disciples:”) and the imperative address (“Happen you know this!”) as later framing/application voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core rationale is cosmological (like attracts like; purification of the three earths by drawing up their congeners), but introduced by a didactic dialogue header.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.113⟩
Now, first of all, he discharged the water, the waste, the poison of the rulers who are above. He cleansed the firmaments of the [water ... ] he poured down the dark waters. [Just as the] waters fell from heaven to earth, so also the waters below in the earths were drawn and came up from below towards the waters that had come from above to the earths. The waters [were] purified of the dark poison that exists in them. Then he swept them outside and made them a great vessel and a wall of sea that surrounds the universe, and on which the ships sail.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Ordered procedural exposition (“first of all… then…”) with intra-cosmic mechanics and architecture (sea-wall vessel around the universe). No institutional or scriptural overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: After the water, he discharged the darkness. He purified the firmaments and dried from them the darkness with which they are weighed down. He discharged it down to the earth. Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths. The darkness that is in the earths was drawn up towards the darkness that had been discharged from above. He swept them both out and shut them in that [ ... ] of darkness [ ... / ... ] the water.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Parallelism and ‘as above/so below’ mechanics remain internal to the cosmological system; the paragraph is a clean continuation of the technical purification sequence.

paragraphs.core_text: And he discharged the fire from heaven to earth, [ ... at] that time again the fire that was shut [in] the earth below was drawn and came up towards its kind. Fire was added to fire. Afterwards, he swept it out and cast it into the outer underworld, which [he had constructed for] them outside the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate logic: kind draws to kind; accumulation and removal; construction of an external containment realm (“outer underworld”)—cosmic engineering language.

paragraphs.core_text: In the same way that he purified the firmaments above as a place for the light-givers to journey [ ... / ... ] so also he purified the earths below and swept from them the fire and the darkness and the water [ ... ] He has purified them for the ascent of these three powers, they of the wind and the water and the fire, which ascend before the Porter and traverse the earths.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree-structured purification culminating in ascent-pathways for the three light powers; “the Porter” functions as a cosmic agent within the system, not a church office.
